gaps.sentence: Mozart was the greatest ___ (MUSIC) of his age.
gaps.explanation: The suffix -ian forms the person: music becomes musician.

gaps.sentence: When the costs rose, we had to ___ our plans (CONSIDER).
gaps.explanation: The prefix re- means again: reconsider means to think about something again. A base verb follows 'had to'.

gaps.sentence: I'm afraid your passport is ___ — it expired last month (VALID).
gaps.hint: negative adjective needed: it has expired
gaps.explanation: An expired document is invalid (in- + valid); an adjective is needed after 'is'.

gaps.sentence: Be careful not to ___ the medicine — read the label twice (USE).
gaps.explanation: The prefix mis- means wrongly: misuse means to use something incorrectly. A base verb follows 'not to'.

gaps.sentence: The thunderstorm was absolutely ___ , so the children hid under the blankets (TERRIFY).
gaps.hint: the storm causes the fear (-ing); note 'terrific' means excellent
gaps.explanation: The storm causes terror, so it is terrifying; the children felt terrified. 'Terrific' means excellent.
The suffix -en forms verbs from adjectives: thicken. A base verb follows 'to'.

gaps.sentence: She has been a loyal ___ (EMPLOY) of the firm for twenty years.
gaps.hint: person needed: someone who works for the firm
gaps.explanation: An employee works for a company; 'employment' is the uncountable state of having a job.

gaps.sentence: Her suitcase was ___ , so the airline charged extra (WEIGHT).
gaps.hint: weighing too much — that is why she paid extra (over-)
gaps.explanation: The prefix over- means too much: overweight explains the extra charge.
